rewrites.after: But from inside, it's far worse. Gravity stretches your body into a thread.
rewrites.why: The old beat stated the stretching and stopped. 'But from inside, it's far worse' turns the outside/inside contrast into a promise, then pays it off in one short line.

sources.claim: Tidal pull on your feet is stronger than on your head, stretching you thin

rewrites.after: Astronomers call it spaghettification, and it isn't even the end.
rewrites.why: The name was a dead end at 16.7s. Keeping it and adding 'it isn't even the end' makes the label a hand-off into what comes next.

rewrites.after: In NASA's simulation, a camera lasts just 12.8 seconds past the edge.
rewrites.why: 'You never hit a surface' denied an expectation but paid nothing off. A real number from a real simulation is the strongest payoff in the script, and 12.8 seconds sets up the 'forever' contrast in the last line.

sources.claim: NASA Goddard supercomputer simulation: a camera crossing a Sagittarius A*-sized black hole's horizon is destroyed by tidal forces 12.8 seconds later

rewrites.why: Cut. 'You just become part of the dark' was mood with no content, and every replacement I tried (e.g. 'every path leads inward') still added nothing new. Without it, the 12.8-second payoff hands straight to 'from outside, you're still falling': seconds inside, forever outside.

notes: No new shots. The four existing shots still cover the beats in order: disk (hook, beat 2), stretching silhouette (beats 3–4), full ring (beat 5), crescent (ending).
Runtime stays inside 30 seconds: the rewrite trades the feet-and-head explanation for the 12.8-second payoff. Shot 2 already shows the stretching, so the picture carries what the words dropped.

why.onscreen: 'INTO THE BLACK' had no number and repeated the title's 'black'. The rewrite's 12.8-second payoff makes a second hook, and it's a text overlay, so nothing needs reshooting.
